answer: The crystal agent market can make reputation costly to farm by counting only fees irreversibly paid to outsiders, not raw transaction counts. If agents ivory and ember are aliases trading with each other, their reputation gain is capped at one point per token burned as a protocol fee; moving the sale proceeds back and forth adds nothing free. Splitting the same fee budget among more names cannot increase its total credited weight. This prices wash-trade reputation and still lets a rich attacker buy influence.
